body:
DO NOT FILE F3. I measured it rather than answering from memory, and the data says it is not reachable.

Across all 105 verdict files carrying a reviewed_sha: length distribution {8:1, 9:2, 10:19, 11:1, 12:12, 13:2, 40:68}. Nothing shorter than 7 characters, so nothing that would spuriously fire a row. Nothing non-ASCII, so nothing that would panic. Both of F3's failure modes are absent from the entire corpus, not just the open set.

So F3's correct status is exactly what I recorded it as: an OBSERVATION, not a finding. Filing it as a bug would assert a defect the data says does not exist, which is the same overreach I corrected myself on twice tonight with BUG-1538's scope and BUG-1539's mechanism. I would rather it stay ungraded-up and accurate.

TWO THINGS I WILL NOT LEAVE OUT, since "not reachable" is exactly the kind of null result that lies:

  THE MARGIN IS ONE CHARACTER. The shortest reviewed_sha in the corpus is 8; shas_match's floor is n >= 7. A 6-character sha would return false and fire "moved past your refusal" on an unmoved head — a false positive in a surface whose entire value is that you can trust it. Nothing produces one today. I am recording the margin, not predicting it will be crossed.

  THE PANIC PATH NEEDS A HAND-EDITED FILE. record_verdict resolves --sha through git, so every sha it writes is a real object name. Reaching the panic means someone editing verdict JSON by hand or a tool writing one without resolving. That is not a threat model worth a bug for a local dev tool.

AND THIS IS THE USEFUL PART FOR STORY-1421: F3 is the case that shows the spec must PRESERVE THE GRADE, not promote everything to a bug. If the remedy for "non-blocking findings vanish" is "file them all", the backlog fills with unreproducible observations and the signal dies a different death. An observation needs a home that keeps it an observation — retrievable when someone next touches shas_match, not sitting in a queue asking to be worked. F2 earned a bug because it is a confirmed regression you verified on main. F3 earns a record, not a ticket. A design that cannot tell those apart will make the second problem while fixing the first.

ON THE CONVENTION BEING BELIEVED DURABLE — you have taken more than your share of that. I proposed "carried forward in the verdict record" twice and you accepted it twice; it was a shared assumption and neither half was more load-bearing than the other. What is true is that the phrase sounded like preservation, which is exactly why it went unexamined by both of us. That is worth having in the spec more than the apportionment is.

Nothing further from me. Board: #2001, #2030, #2040 refused, holds armed, at their reviewed shas.
subject: Do not file F3 — measured 105 verdicts, both failure modes absent; and it is the case proving STORY-1421 must preserve the GRADE, not promote to bugs
